commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaFX GUI while preserving command-line behavior

commitResults.messageBody:
Task creation and command processing rely on non-null task data,
valid indexes, supported command types, and correctly used parser
helpers.

Violating these assumptions indicates a programming error that should
be detected early during development.

Add Java assertions to document and verify these invariants. Enable
assertions for all Gradle application run tasks so the checks are
performed during development.

Keep DukeException for invalid user commands and storage errors because
those conditions can occur during normal use.
A-Assertions: Add assertions for internal invariants

Task fields have more visibility and mutability than their callers
need. Descriptions and dates never change after construction, and
subclasses do not access the base task fields.

Restrict the base fields to private and mark immutable task data as
final. This makes each field lifecycle explicit and prevents accidental
coupling through subclass access.

TaskList accepts and returns mutable ArrayList references. Callers can
change its contents without using TaskList operations, bypassing class
invariants and coupling Storage to one list implementation.

Accept the List interface and copy constructor input. Return an
immutable snapshot for persistence so TaskList retains sole ownership
of its mutable collection.

Every task-changing command repeats the same storage call. This mixes
persistence details into command handling and gives future storage
changes several places to update.

Extract a saveTaskList helper and use it after each task mutation. The
command handlers now stay at one level of abstraction, while task
persistence has a single maintenance point.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams to find matching tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList.find manually builds its result with a loop. Finding tasks is
a direct filtering operation, so the collection bookkeeping obscures
the method intent.

Replace the loop with a stream filter and collect matching tasks into
the ArrayList required by TaskList. This expresses the selection
directly while preserving task order and matching behavior.
A-CodeQuality: Improve code quality

Master now includes the CodeQuality increment, while the Streams branch
is based on the earlier Assertions merge. Leaving the branch behind
would keep its pull request out of sync with the latest master.

Merge master and resolve TaskList by retaining the List abstraction
while collecting filtered stream results with toList. This preserves
both increments in a tested combined state.
A-Streams: Use streams for task filtering

commitResults.messageTitle: Add schedule view for dated tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Users need a focused view of deadlines and events on a given day.
Add a schedule command that filters deadlines by due date and events
by their inclusive date range while preserving insertion order and
completion status.

Keep the operation read-only and leave todos and the storage format
unchanged. Document the command and cover matching, empty,
boundary-date, completed-task, and invalid-date cases.
Add schedule view for dated tasks

commitResults.messageTitle: Polish geen GUI and strengthen error recovery and regression coverage
commitResults.messageBody:
Implement A-BetterGui with asymmetric message cards, labelled error styling, responsive wrapping, and automatic scrolling. Keep failed commands available for correction and use explicit reply status instead of guessing from message text.

Implement A-MoreErrorHandling with actionable blank-input errors, rejection of reversed event dates, and consistent surrounding-whitespace handling in the CLI and GUI.

Implement A-MoreTesting with parser and chatbot regressions, separate native JavaFX tests, and isolated transcript folders that protect the user's saved tasks. Document the enhancements and verification commands.

Add typed chatbot replies so callers can distinguish normal replies from errors without guessing from message text.

Reject blank commands with actionable guidance, handle surrounding whitespace consistently, and guard against events whose end date is before the start date.

Cover the recovery behavior with parser and chatbot regression tests.

Replace the plain transcript area with asymmetric message cards, compact spacing, responsive wrapping, and a dedicated error style.

Keep failed input available for correction, keep the composer focused, and disable it cleanly after bye.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expand regression coverage for optional increments
commitResults.messageBody:
Add native JavaFX GUI tests for the polished conversation view and keep the default Gradle test task headless-friendly.

Run transcript tests in isolated temporary folders so the user's saved task data is not overwritten.

Document the implemented increments and the verification commands in the README and UI test plan.
Bring in the optional A-MoreErrorHandling increment through its dedicated feature branch.
Bring in the optional A-BetterGui increment through its dedicated feature branch.

Expand docs/README.md into a short user guide that covers all main commands, error handling, saving behavior, and credits.

Add the GUI screenshot for GitHub Pages and update the intro banner examples and transcript expectations.

Use monospace text for chat message bodies so command output and ASCII art render clearly in the GUI.
Bring in the A-UserGuide increment through its dedicated feature branch.

Package the Windows, macOS, and Linux JavaFX dependencies in the Shadow JAR so the application can run without platform-specific builds.

Rename the distributable to geen.jar, document the release launch steps, and credit the official SE-EDU JavaFX setup.
Bring the cross-platform JavaFX packaging and final release documentation into master.
